verdict: The feed is the weakest part of Techgist, and the owner is right that it doesn't feel like a real news product. I checked the live edition (published 2026-11-11 03:30Z, 226 stories). The server computes a ranking, but the app throws it away and shows every tab newest-first (NewsStore.swift:47). The Top tab isn't curated either: it holds all 91 stories from the 10 general feeds plus 13 picks, 104 cards in all. It opens with a future-dated OpenAI customer case study, then two random DEV.to posts, then Engadget explainers like "What is the average lifespan of recordable Blu-ray discs?" and "Why your Roku might be plugged into the wrong HDMI port". Clustering matches headline words only, so it misses the day's two big stories. The Anthropic IPO appears as 10 separate cards (7 in Top) and the Jensen Huang scandal as 9 (7 in Top). The other tabs are stale: the AI tab's median story age is 32.5h, Startups is 43h with stories over 130h old, and Blogs is 160h. Of Techmeme's latest 15 stories, only about 4 are in the edition, missing for example OpenAI's leaked Q3 revenue, the Daylight $80M Series B, the Coframe $25M Series A and the Railway hack. There isn't a single Indian source for an audience that is half Bengaluru. 29% of cards (66/226) have no AI summary and fall back to 0–30-word feed excerpts. Story length isn't consistent either: summaries run 39–99 words and headlines go up to 102 characters, while Inshorts holds a strict 60 words. Compared with Techmeme, Inshorts or Google News Top Stories, it lacks the three things those feeds rest on. First, event-level clustering (one card per event). Second, an importance score that blends how many outlets cover a story, how authoritative they are and how fresh it is, and that actually decides the order. Third, an editorial filter that removes non-news. All three can be built on the existing stack: the cron server, the Nemotron calls already made for each story, and NVIDIA's free embedding endpoint.

findings.title: App discards the ranking: every tab is sorted newest-first
findings.evidence: ios/Techgist/Services/NewsStore.swift:47 `return inTab.sorted { $0.publishedAt > $1.publishedAt }`. Ranker.rank() (Ranker.swift:46-52) carefully orders stories and sets topRank, but the view (Views/ContentView.swift:97) uses articles(in:), which sorts by time. Live Top tab positions 0-5: [OpenAI] Gilbert + Tobin case study (topRank 5, future-dated), [DEV Community] 'One probe tells you nothing…' (topRank 33), [DEV Community] 'LNbits 1.7.0…' (topRank 44), CNBC, TechCrunch 'X launches clipping', Engadget 'average lifespan of Blu-ray discs' (topRank 11). Toyota Kei truck (topRank 0) is at position 19.
findings.recommendation: Order every tab by the server's rank. Ship an explicit `rank` per tab in edition.json (e.g. `ranks: {"Top": 3, "AI": 1}`) and sort by it in articles(in:). Put recency in front of that order with one rule: on open, show stories first seen since the user's last visit and scoring above the tab's median at the top, with a 'New' chip, then the rest in rank order. Move already-read cards (track ids locally) to the end, as Inshorts does with 'unread first'.

findings.title: Story clustering misses the day's biggest events, giving 7+ duplicate cards in Top
findings.evidence: Ranker.swift:125-130 needs at least 3 shared title tokens and an IDF overlap of 0.4 or more. Live: the Anthropic IPO has 10 cards (Guardian $1.4tn, CNBC Australian retail, CNBC Cramer, NYT 'tie it closer to Nvidia', NYT 'Amazon and Google paydays', BBC $1.3tn, TechCrunch 'founders cash out $250M', Decoder roadshow, Latent Space, Stratechery), 7 of them in Top. Jensen Huang/Nvidia spy: 9 cards, 7 in Top. CoreWeave earnings: 2 CNBC cards. Muse Ember: 2. 'Introducing Businesses in ChatGPT' (OpenAI) and Decoder 'ChatGPT business directory': 2. Only 15/226 stories carry alsoCoveredBy.
findings.recommendation: Cluster at the event level on the server: (1) embed headline + first 2 sentences with NVIDIA's hosted embedding model (e.g. nvidia/nv-embedqa-e5-v5, same API key) and treat cosine ≥ 0.80 within 48h as the same event, or 0.72 when the stories also share a named entity; (2) have the existing Nemotron call return an `event_key` slug (e.g. 'anthropic-ipo') and merge clusters with the same key within 72h; (3) keep a persistent cluster store (~/.techshorts/clusters.json) so follow-ups join an existing event. Show one card per event per tab, with the best source as the lead, 'N sources' on the card, and the other angles (Cramer, NYT analysis) as a 'More on this' list. Exception: a follow-up becomes a new card only if the LLM says it adds a material new fact (e.g. 'price range raised').

findings.title: Top tab is uncurated: all 91 general-feed stories plus picks, 104 cards
findings.evidence: Ranker.swift:36 `var topPicks = ranked[.top] ?? []` puts every story from the 10 Top feeds in Top. Live Top includes off-topic and evergreen items: NYT 'Toyota Plans to Sell a Kei Pickup Truck' (topRank 0), NYT 'A Fan-Favorite Aquarium Screen Saver Is Leaving Roku', NYT 'What BlackBerries and Horseshoes Reveal…', Engadget 'What is the Dead Internet Theory', 'How to get this Siri camera upgrade', Wired 'Huupe Mini 2 Review'. Engadget alone has 10 cards and Wired 12.
findings.recommendation: Cap Top at 30 cards selected by score, with no source-category auto-inclusion. Require is_news=true, importance ≥ 6/10 and age ≤ 36h. At most 3 cards per publisher in the top 10 and 5 in the full tab. Hold reviews, explainers and how-tos out of Top entirely (allow them in the other tabs at most once per 10 cards).

findings.title: Scoring formula prefers any fresh post over important news, and dates clusters by the lead's age
findings.evidence: Ranker.swift:64-70 `score = weight * coverageBoost * pointsBoost / (ageHours + 12)`. A DEV Community post (weight 0.4) at 0.1h scores 0.4/12.1 = 0.033, beating a TechCrunch story (weight 1) at 24h: 1/36 = 0.028. That is how two DEV.to posts got into Top (topRanks 33, 44) through topPicksPerTab[.dev]=3 (Ranker.swift:62). The cluster lead keeps its own publishedAt (quality() tie-breaks on earliest, Ranker.swift:73-76), so the 6-outlet Huang cluster led by BBC is 36.7h old although coverage 4h old exists. That also keeps it out of BreakingNews (BreakingNews.swift:31 needs <6h).
findings.recommendation: Replace it with score = I × C × A × F. I = LLM importance 1–10 for 'tech professionals in Bengaluru and Silicon Valley', mapped to (I/10)^1.5. C = 1 + 0.6·log2(publishers in cluster), ×1.5 if the event is on Techmeme, ×(1 + 0.3·log2(HN points/100)) capped at 1.6. A = source authority 0.5–1.2 (Reuters/Bloomberg/TechCrunch/The Information 1.2, The Verge/Ars 1.0, Engadget 0.8, community feeds 0.5). F = exp(-age/τ) with age measured from cluster first_seen, τ = 10h for Top, 18h AI, 24h Startups, 48h Dev, 96h Blogs, plus a 0.5× credit for last_update when new sources joined within 3h. Don't use a 1/(age+12) term with no importance input.

findings.title: Stale tabs: windows of 7 and 45 days and a per-feed limit of 12 fill tabs with old stories
findings.evidence: FeedService.swift:76 `maxAgeDays = blogs ? 45 : 7`, FeedService.swift:8 perFeedLimit 12. Live: AI tab has 40 stories, 23 over 24h, 13 over 48h, median 32.5h. Startups has 28, 24 over 24h, 13 over 48h, median 43.2h, and positions 16-24 are 105–135h old ('Zipline hits $21.5B valuation' at 131.8h). Blogs has 46, 38 over 24h, 22 over 7 days, median 160.5h. Dev is 12 DEV.to posts at 0.1–0.3h, then a jump to 38.5h–157h.
findings.recommendation: Use hard windows per tab: Top 36h, AI 72h, Startups 72h, Dev 7d, Blogs 14d. Tab sizes: Top 30, AI 25, Startups 25, Dev 20, Blogs 15. Drop anything below 25% of the tab's median score instead of padding. When a tab runs short, show 'You're all caught up', not week-old filler.

findings.title: Future-dated items pin themselves to the top
findings.evidence: Live: [OpenAI] 'Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI' publishedAt 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z, which is 20.5h in the future relative to the edition. Because tabs sort by time, it is card #1 in both Top and AI, with no summary and no image. OpenAI's feed gives only a date, and nothing clamps it.
findings.recommendation: In Article(item:) or on the server, clamp publishedAt to min(feedDate, firstSeenAt). Keep a persistent first_seen per URL on the server (~/.techshorts/seen.json) and use first_seen for all freshness math. Feeds that give only a date then can't jump ahead of real news.

findings.title: Source mix is wrong for the audience: no Indian sources, no Techmeme, too many low-signal feeds
findings.evidence: ios/Techgist/Models/FeedSource.swift:29-61 lists 27 feeds, none of them Indian. Low-signal feeds: DEV Community (12 cards, all 10 top Dev slots, 2 in Top), Product Hunt (12 cards with names like 'Clive', 'Obsiva', 'ZUS', 0 summaries, 0 images), the OpenAI blog (12 cards, mostly customer stories, 0 summaries, 0 images). Coverage gap: of the 15 latest Techmeme items (2026-11-10), Techgist has about 4. Missing: OpenAI Q3 revenue/margin leak, Daylight $80M Series B, Coframe $25M Series A, Railway hack report, Cash App founder murder sentencing, Commerce Entity List delay, NSA/Cyber Command report, mobile-gaming analysis. Checked working feeds: techmeme.com/feed.xml, inc42.com/feed/, yourstory.com/feed, economictimes.indiatimes.com/tech/rssfeeds/13357270.cms, moneycontrol.com/rss/technology.xml, theinformation.com/feed, semafor.com/rss.xml, 404media.co/rss/, platformer.news/rss/, huggingface.co/blog/feed.xml, techcrunch.com/category/artificial-intelligence/feed/ (all HTTP 200).
findings.recommendation: Add Techmeme as a signal feed: match its linked URLs and entities to clusters for the ×1.5 boost, and import its funding/leak items where no other source has them, summarized from the linked article. Add an India group: Inc42, YourStory, ET Tech, Moneycontrol Tech, plus Entrackr/The Ken headlines as signal. Add TechCrunch AI, Semafor Tech and The Information (headline signal only, paywalled). Drop DEV Community. Reduce Product Hunt to the day's top 3 by votes, or drop it. Let OpenAI/Google AI posts through only when LLM triage marks them as a product/model launch, not a customer story or 'Academy' post. Add a 'Region: India / US / Both' setting that multiplies score by 1.3 for matching region tags, so Bengaluru users see Indian funding and policy news.

findings.title: 29% of cards have no Techgist summary; fallback excerpts are 0–30 words
findings.evidence: Live: 160/226 have headline+summary, 66 don't. By source: OpenAI 12/12, Product Hunt 12/12, NYT 8, Wired 4, Latent Space 4, HN 3, TechCrunch 3. Fallback excerpt word counts include 0, 5, 6, 7, 7, 7… with median about 25. NYT and OpenAI are blocked or paywalled, so article_text() returns the feed text and enrich.py:124 skips anything under 40 words ('too little text'). That skip is cached permanently (enrich.py:179-180). 36 stories lack an image (OpenAI 12, Product Hunt 12, Simon Willison 6, HN 4).
findings.recommendation: Make 'has a 55–65-word summary' a requirement for Top and AI/Startups. If the article text is blocked, summarize from the fullest text in the same cluster (the Anthropic NYT angle has 6 sibling articles). If the story is unique and under 40 words, either exclude it or show it in a compact 'headline-only' style, never as a full card. Retry 'too little text' skips once after 2h. For missing images, fetch og:image server-side for every story (already done for some), then fall back to a generated branded card (source logo + headline) instead of an empty card.

findings.title: Story size is inconsistent: summaries 39–99 words, headlines up to 102 chars
findings.evidence: Live summaries: min 39, p10 48, median 65, p90 89, max 99 words. enrich.py:129 accepts 35–100 words and headlines up to 110 chars, although the prompt asks for 55–70 words and ≤90 chars (enrich.py:29-33). Headlines: median 69 chars, max 102, 24 over 80 chars. Inshorts uses at most 60 words and about 60–70-char headlines so every card fits one screen with the image.
findings.recommendation: Tighten the prompt to '50–60 words, 3 sentences: what happened; key numbers/who; why it matters to builders/investors' and the headline to '≤70 characters'. Enforce 48–62 words and ≤75 chars in validation. On failure, retry once with the measured length fed back ('your summary was 84 words; cut to 58'), not falling back to the excerpt. Measure fit against the smallest supported screen (iPhone SE/mini) in CardView and reject summaries that overflow.

findings.title: LLM headlines sometimes misrepresent the story or drop attribution
findings.evidence: Live: CNBC 'Jim Cramer says Anthropic's explosive growth could justify a record-breaking IPO' became 'Anthropic files IPO paperwork for up to $64.35 billion raise', turning an opinion piece into a hard-news claim. Simon Willison's 'llm-gemini 0.36' (a plugin release note) became 'Google Gemini 4 Carbon launched for all users with new pricing tiers' and sits in Top (topRank 17) under Simon Willison, duplicating The Decoder's real story. The grounded() check (enrich.py:89-98) only checks numbers and capitalized words, so it can't catch a change of subject or a missing attribution.
findings.recommendation: Add to the prompt: 'If the piece is opinion, analysis, an interview or a release note, the headline must say so (e.g. "Cramer: …", "Analysis: …")'. Add a faithfulness gate: the cosine similarity between the embeddings of the new headline and the original title must be ≥ 0.55, else fall back to the original title. Have the LLM return `type` (news/analysis/opinion/interview/review/tutorial/release_notes/promo/podcast) and show non-news types with a small label.

findings.title: Categories come from the source, not the story
findings.evidence: Article.category = source.category (FeedService.swift:115). Live: the Anthropic IPO (Guardian, CNBC, BBC, NYT, TechCrunch) never reaches the AI or Startups tab. 'Claude Fable 5.2 review' (Lenny's) is in Startups. The Jensen Huang affair (Stratechery) is in Blogs. The Startups tab has only 3 sources (TechCrunch Startups, Product Hunt, Lenny's) and just 4 stories under 24h, while funding news from Techmeme (Daylight, Coframe) is absent.
findings.recommendation: Have the existing enrichment call return `topics` (multi-label from: ai, startups_funding, bigtech, dev_tools, security, policy, hardware, india, science, consumer). Assign tab membership from topics, so a story can appear in Top and AI. Keep the source category only as a prior. A Startups tab built on 'startups_funding' from all sources (TechCrunch, Inc42, YourStory, Techmeme) would show 10–20 fresh rounds and acquisitions a day.

findings.title: Junk filter is a deals-only regex; explainers, reviews, podcasts and link-blog fragments pass
findings.evidence: FeedService.swift:123-142 ContentFilter catches only deals, coupons, sponsored posts and TechCrunch events. Live items that passed: Engadget 'What is the average lifespan of recordable Blu-ray discs?', 'Why your Roku might be plugged into the wrong HDMI port', 'How to get this Siri camera upgrade…', Wired 'Huupe Mini 2 Review', Martin Fowler 'Fragments: November 10/October 28/21/4', Simon Willison 'Quoting Nilay Patel', 'Quoting Prompting Claude Fable 5.2', 'Terry Pratchett's Study', Pragmatic Engineer 'The Pragmatic Summit 2027' (event promo), Latent Space podcast episodes ('Designing for Agents — Zeno Rocha, Resend'), DEV.to tutorials ('How to Use a Proxy in Python requests').
findings.recommendation: Move triage into the LLM call (it already runs once per story): {is_news, type, importance, topics, region, event_key}, with a short rubric plus 10 few-shot examples taken from this edition. Keep the regex as a cheap pre-filter and add patterns: '^(what|why|how) (is|your|to)\b', '\breview:?\b', '^fragments:', '^quoting ', 'podcast|episode|\| [A-Z].*\(.*Head of', 'summit 20\d\d'. Before the LLM step, skip titles under 3 words (e.g. Product Hunt 'Clive', 'ZUS').

findings.title: Social-signal boost almost never fires
findings.evidence: server/main.swift:68-104 matches Reddit only on exact links from one combined top-100 RSS. Live: only 2 stories carry 'Reddit' in alsoCoveredBy. HN points exist on only 12 stories (hnrss frontpage?points=150).
findings.recommendation: Match Reddit and HN links to clusters (any member URL or embedding match), not to single URLs. Also count Techmeme presence, which is the strongest free importance signal for this audience. Use hnrss.org/newest?points=50 for an earlier HN signal and weight it by points velocity (points/hour since first seen).

findings.title: Breaking-news selection depends on the broken clustering and the lead's date
findings.evidence: BreakingNews.swift:30-31 needs topRank, at least 3 outlets and lead age under 6h. Live: the biggest event (Anthropic IPO, 10 articles) shows at most 2 outlets on any card ('Anthropic targets valuation…' alsoCoveredBy=[New York Times]), so it never qualifies. The Huang cluster has 7 outlets, but its lead is 36.7h old, so it doesn't qualify either.
findings.recommendation: Compute alert candidates on the server from event clusters: importance ≥ 8, at least 4 distinct publishers or on Techmeme, and cluster first_seen < 2h. Write them into the edition (`alerts: [{eventKey, headline, summary, image}]`) with at most 2–3 per day and quiet hours based on the user's region (IST/PT). The client then only decides whether to show them. (Delivery timing is a separate topic: BGAppRefresh can't deliver on time.)

verdict:
The app is a competent SwiftUI prototype, but it does not yet look like a polished news product. It has one card template (ios/Techgist/Views/CardView.swift, 136 lines), one vertically paged ScrollView, and system sheets for everything else. It uses none of the iOS 17 polish APIs: grep finds zero uses of sensoryFeedback, scrollTransition, symbolEffect, matchedGeometryEffect, contextMenu, redacted or a navigation transition. So the app has no haptics, no card-to-card motion, no skeletons and no micro-interactions. These are exactly the things that make Inshorts, Apple News and Particle feel premium.

The larger problem is that the screen does not control its content. Live summaries run from 39 to 99 words (average 67), and 21 stories exceed 85 words. They are forced into a fixed-height card with .lineLimit(10).minimumScaleFactor(0.85). The result is shrunken, truncated text on most phones. At the other extreme, 14 stories (mostly Product Hunt) are a 1–2 word headline with a 5–10 word excerpt floating in an empty card. 36 of 226 stories (16%) have no photo, including all 12 OpenAI and 12 Product Hunt items. These get a gradient with the publisher's name in 34pt heavy type, which looks like a placeholder.

The Top tab sorts by publishedAt (NewsStore.swift:47) instead of by topRank. On the live edition (published 2026-11-11 03:30Z), the first card a user sees is therefore an OpenAI customer-story post: "Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI". It is dated 20 hours in the future, so the card shows "in 20 hours". It has a gradient cover and a 13-word excerpt, and it sits ahead of the Starlink, Pixel Tag and Anthropic IPO stories that the ranker put at #1–#7.

Fixing the card's size contract, the first-screen ordering, source identity, image loading and motion/haptics would close most of the gap with Inshorts. That is about 1–2 weeks of SwiftUI work and needs no new infrastructure. A WidgetKit widget, a proper reader screen and rich notifications would close the rest.

findings.title: Card has no size contract: 99-word summaries are shrunk and cut off, and 5-word excerpts float in empty cards
findings.evidence: CardView.swift:36-41 uses Text(summary).font(.body).lineLimit(10).minimumScaleFactor(0.85) inside a card fixed to the container height (ContentView.swift:118 .containerRelativeFrame(.vertical)). Live edition: summary word counts are min 39 / max 99 / mean 66.7, and 21 summaries are over 85 words (e.g. Verge Starlink 99, CNBC 99, HN Glasswing 99). On an iPhone 15/16 (852pt screen) the feed area is about 667pt. The image takes 0.32 of that, about 213pt (CardView.swift:14). After padding, the source row, a 3–4 line title3 headline and the action row, roughly 230pt is left for body text: about 10 lines at 17pt, or about 80 words at 325pt width. Anything longer gets scaled to 85% and then cut with an ellipsis. Meanwhile 14 stories without summaries have excerpts of 0–13 words (e.g. Product Hunt 'LotusQ': 'Talk instead of type, in any app'; HN 'AMD's Zen 6 Family': 'Hello you fine Internet folks,'; HN 'Show HN: Valencia…': empty). The share text also promises 'tech news in 60 words' (ShareCard.swift:24, :70), which these summaries contradict. Inshorts enforces a hard 60-word body that always fits without truncation.
findings.recommendation: Set a hard size contract and design the card to it. (1) On the server, cap summaries at 55–62 words and headlines at 70 characters, and reject or regenerate anything outside that range. (2) In CardView, remove minimumScaleFactor. Use Text(summary).font(.system(size: 17, weight: .regular)).lineSpacing(5).foregroundStyle(.primary.opacity(0.82)) with no lineLimit for 60 words, and keep lineLimit(9) only as a safety net. (3) Add a CardLayout enum chosen per article: .standard (photo plus 60 words), .compact (short excerpt under 25 words: larger headline in .title.bold, excerpt in .title3, no empty space) and .launch (Product Hunt: app-icon-style tile, tagline, maker link). Better still, group Product Hunt items into one 'Launches today' card with a horizontal ScrollView of 5–6 rows. (4) Drop any story whose body is under 15 words and has no image. Do not show 'Hello you fine Internet folks,' as news.

findings.title: First screen shows the wrong story: Top ignores topRank, and future-dated items show 'in 20 hours'
findings.evidence: NewsStore.swift:47 returns inTab.sorted { $0.publishedAt > $1.publishedAt } for every tab, including Top, so the server's topRank is thrown away for display. Live edition: the OpenAI item 'Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI' is dated 20.5h after the edition's publishedAt (topRank 5). It therefore becomes card #1 of Top and of AI. It shows the OpenAI gradient cover (no image), a 13-word excerpt, and CardView.swift:26 renders .relative(presentation: .named) as 'in 20 hours'. The real #1–#4 stories (Kei truck, Starlink Mini 2, Ring drone, Glasswing CVEs) come after it. Stale items also stay in tabs: 30+ AI, Startups and Dev items are 100–159 hours old, and one is 887h old.
findings.recommendation: Sort Top by topRank (ascending), and sort other tabs by a blended score instead of raw date. Within the first 10 cards, keep at least 6 stories under 12h old. Clamp the displayed date with min(article.publishedAt, Date()), and drop items dated more than 1h in the future. Replace the timestamp with a compact format, e.g. a helper that returns '12m', '3h', 'Yesterday' or 'Nov 4' via Date.RelativeFormatStyle(presentation: .numeric, unitsStyle: .narrow). For any tab, hide items over 72h old unless the tab would otherwise have fewer than 15 cards.

findings.title: No motion and no haptics anywhere: paging feels like a plain list
findings.evidence: grep over ios/Techgist finds no sensoryFeedback, UIImpactFeedbackGenerator, scrollTransition, symbolEffect, matchedGeometryEffect or visualEffect. Paging is a bare .scrollTargetBehavior(.paging) (ContentView.swift:132). The bookmark toggles with no animation (CardView.swift:58-60). Tab switches use .animation(.default) (ContentView.swift:29). The 'new stories' pill has no haptic (ContentView.swift:32). Inshorts gives a stacked-card slide with depth. Apple News and Particle use haptic ticks on selection, a bookmark bounce, and parallax hero images.
findings.recommendation: Add these, all iOS 17 APIs. (a) Card depth on paging: on CardView inside the LazyVStack, use .scrollTransition(.interactive, axis: .vertical) { c, p in c.scaleEffect(p.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.92).opacity(p.isIdentity ? 1 : 0.5).offset(y: p.value * -40) }. (b) Image parallax: on ArticleImage, use .visualEffect { c, proxy in c.offset(y: -proxy.frame(in: .scrollView).minY * 0.15) }, with the image 15% taller than its frame. (c) Track the current card with .scrollPosition(id: $currentID) and add .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: currentID). (d) Bookmark: Image(systemName:).contentTransition(.symbolEffect(.replace)) plus .symbolEffect(.bounce, value: isSaved) plus .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: isSaved). (e) Category change: .sensoryFeedback(.selection, trigger: store.category), and a matchedGeometryEffect underline or capsule that slides between chips instead of recolouring. (f) New-stories pill: .sensoryFeedback(.impact(weight: .light), trigger: waiting?.newCount) when it appears, and .spring(response: 0.4, dampingFraction: 0.8) when it inserts. (g) Pull-to-refresh done: .sensoryFeedback(.success, trigger: lastUpdated).

findings.title: No source identity: blue uppercase text in place of logos, and 16% of stories get a gradient that reads as a placeholder
findings.evidence: CardView.swift:19 shows only Text(article.source.uppercased()).bold().foregroundStyle(.tint), with no publisher logo or favicon. StoryCover (CardView.swift:106-135) fills the photo slot with a category gradient and the source name in .largeTitle heavy. In the live edition 36/226 stories have no image: all 12 OpenAI, all 12 Product Hunt, 6 Simon Willison, 4 Hacker News, 2 NYT. The '+N more' chip (line 20-24) is plain text and cannot be tapped, even though 15 live stories carry alsoCoveredBy. Google News and Particle show stacked publisher favicons and open a 'Full coverage' view when tapped.
findings.recommendation: Bundle a 64×64 logo asset for each of the 27 FeedSource entries (a one-time job). Render HStack(spacing: 6) { Image(source.logo).resizable().frame(width: 18, height: 18).clipShape(.rect(cornerRadius: 4)); Text(source).font(.footnote.weight(.semibold)) }, with the time in .footnote .secondary. Make '+3 more' a Button that opens a .presentationDetents([.medium]) sheet listing each covering outlet's logo, name and link, with 3 overlapping 16pt logo circles as the label. For image-less stories, replace the giant-text gradient with either (a) the og:image the server fetches from the article page or (b) a branded 'quote card': publisher logo at 44pt, a pull-quote of the first summary sentence in .title3 serif, on a subtle tinted .ultraThinMaterial background. Use the compact card layout when neither is available.

findings.title: Typography is flat: 20pt headline, gray body, no editorial voice
findings.evidence: CardView.swift:32 sets the headline to .title3.weight(.bold) (20pt) with lineLimit(4). The body (line 38-39) is .body in .secondary gray, which lowers contrast for the main content. The source row is .caption (12pt). Live headlines average 64 characters, with outliers up to 102 (Glasswing, Google Cloud healthcare, Git 2.56.1), which wrap to 4 lines at 20pt. Inshorts uses about 22pt medium headlines with a near-black body. Apple News uses large serif/sans pairings, and Artifact and Particle use 24–28pt display headlines.
findings.recommendation: Headline: .font(.system(.title2, design: .serif, weight: .bold)), 22pt and scaling with Dynamic Type, with .lineSpacing(2) and .lineLimit(3). Combine this with the server's 70-character cap. Body: .font(.system(.body)) with .lineSpacing(5) and .foregroundStyle(Color.primary.opacity(0.85)) instead of .secondary. Meta row: .footnote (13pt). Spacing: 14pt between meta and headline, 10pt between headline and body, 20pt horizontal padding. Show the 'Summarized by AI' label (line 43-47, .caption2 .tertiary) as a small sparkles glyph beside the timestamp so it does not take a separate line.

findings.title: Card proportions: the inset 'card in a list' wastes width, and the 'bigger photo on tall phones' branch only fires on Max/Plus models
findings.evidence: CardView.swift:14 sets image height to height * (height > 700 ? 0.4 : 0.32), where height is the feed container height. On a 6.1in iPhone 15/16 that is about 852 - 59 status - 44 nav - ~48 chip bar - 34 home ≈ 667pt, so it takes the 0.32 branch (~213pt). Only 6.7in phones (container ~747pt) get 0.4. Lines 80-83 add a 22pt corner radius, a black 0.08 shadow (invisible in dark mode), 16pt horizontal and 10pt vertical padding, so the photo is 361pt wide instead of 393pt and the crop ratio changes per device. Inshorts and Google News Newscasts use full-bleed cards, with the image edge to edge at about 42% of screen height.
findings.recommendation: Make the card full-bleed: no horizontal padding or outer shadow, background Color(.systemBackground). Size the image by width, not container height: .aspectRatio(16/10, contentMode: .fill), giving about 246pt on a 393pt-wide phone. Add a LinearGradient(colors: [.clear, .black.opacity(0.35)], startPoint: .center, endPoint: .bottom) scrim so a source logo badge can sit on the photo. Keep at most a 12pt rounded bottom corner via .clipShape(UnevenRoundedRectangle(bottomLeadingRadius: 12, bottomTrailingRadius: 12)). Separate cards with a 1px divider, or use the scrollTransition depth effect in place of shadows.

findings.title: Image loading: AsyncImage with no prefetch, no downsampling and no skeleton, so photos pop in over a name-gradient
findings.evidence: ArticleImage (CardView.swift:87-103) overlays AsyncImage on StoryCover. While the photo loads, the user sees the big gradient with the publisher name, then it cross-fades in 0.2s, so the image visibly flashes on every swipe. Only the next article's metadata is prepared (ContentView.swift:120-125); its image is not prefetched. The only cache is URLCache (TechgistApp.swift:11). AsyncImage decodes at full size on the main render path. The server already produces 720px JPEGs.
findings.recommendation: Write a small ImageLoader actor: an NSCache<NSURL, UIImage> plus URLSession data plus UIImage.byPreparingThumbnail(ofSize: CGSize(width: 393*3, height: 246*3)) off the main thread. Prefetch images for index+1…index+3 from the onAppear on line 120. While loading, show a neutral Color(.secondarySystemFill) block with a shimmer (a LinearGradient mask animated with .repeatForever(autoreverses: false)), not StoryCover. Only show the fallback cover after a failure. Fade in with .transition(.opacity.animation(.easeOut(duration: 0.25))).

findings.title: Reading the full article: SFSafariViewController in a SwiftUI .sheet, and the card body cannot be tapped
findings.evidence: ContentView.swift:62-63 and SupportViews.swift:47 present SafariView via .sheet(item:). This gives a card-style sheet whose swipe-down conflicts with Safari's scrolling, plus a double 'Done' affordance. Reader mode is not requested (SupportViews.swift:9 uses SFSafariViewController(url:) with no Configuration). Only the 'Read full story' button opens the article; tapping the headline, image or body does nothing. Inshorts uses swipe-left or a footer bar ('more at TechCrunch'); Apple News opens a native reader.
findings.recommendation: Present with .fullScreenCover, or wrap SFSafariViewController so it presents modally from UIKit (like StoryShare.present) with modalPresentationStyle = .pageSheet. Build it with let c = SFSafariViewController.Configuration(); c.entersReaderIfAvailable = true; c.barCollapsingEnabled = true, and set preferredControlTintColor = UIColor(named: "AccentColor"). Make the whole text block a tap target (.contentShape(Rectangle()).onTapGesture(perform: onRead)). Replace the bottom 'Read full story' text button with an Inshorts-style footer bar: full width, 44pt, .ultraThinMaterial, showing '[logo] Read more at The Verge ›'. Mark the story read and record dwell time for ranking.

findings.title: Horizontal swipe changes category: a hidden, accidental-prone gesture with no position feedback
findings.evidence: ContentView.swift:22-28 wraps each tab's vertical paging feed in TabView(.page). A slightly diagonal vertical swipe can flip to the next category, and nothing tells the user how many stories remain or where they are. The view keeps no read state, does not dim seen stories, and does not resume where you left off. Each launch starts at card 1, and showWaitingStories also forces scroll-to-top (NewsStore.swift:132).
findings.recommendation: Keep the chip bar as the way to switch categories. Either remove the paged TabView and switch content with .transition(.push(from: selection > old ? .trailing : .leading)), or keep it and add .simultaneousGesture handling so vertical drags win. Add a thin progress indicator, e.g. a 2pt Capsule at the top of the card that fills by currentIndex/count, or '4 of 38' in .caption2 .tertiary. Persist a readIDs Set and the last visible ID per category, and restore it with .scrollPosition(id:) on launch. Show an 'Unread' dot on chips that have new stories.

findings.title: Launch and first-run: blank launch screen, a spinner instead of a skeleton, and no onboarding or topic picking
findings.evidence: Techgist-Info.plist has <key>UILaunchScreen</key><dict/>, so the app launches to a blank white or black screen. With an empty cache, CategoryFeed shows ProgressView("Fetching today's stories…") (ContentView.swift:100). There is no onboarding. The notification ask appears as a .medium sheet after a hard-coded 20s (ContentView.swift:74-81) and can interrupt mid-read. Apple News, Google News and Particle open with a branded launch, a 2–3 screen topic picker, and the notification ask inside onboarding.
findings.recommendation: Set UILaunchScreen to { UIColorName: "LaunchBackground", UIImageName: "Logo" } so the brand shows immediately. Bundle a seed edition.json snapshot in the app so the first launch is never empty. While loading, render 2 skeleton cards with .redacted(reason: .placeholder) and a shimmer. Add a 3-step first-run flow behind @AppStorage("onboarded"): (1) the value prop with a sample card animation, (2) topic chips (AI, Startups, Dev, Big Tech, India tech, Product launches) and a region toggle (Bengaluru / Bay Area) that feed ranking, (3) the notification pre-prompt showing a mock rich notification, with a pick for 'Morning brief at 8:30'. Remove the 20-second timer.

findings.title: Notifications look generic: source name as title, no image, no grouping, no actions
findings.evidence: BreakingNews.swift:47-51 sets content.title to '\(story.source) + N more' and content.body to the headline, with content.sound = .default. It has no attachments, subtitle, threadIdentifier, categoryIdentifier, relevanceScore or interruptionLevel, and is local-only from BGAppRefresh. DailyDigest.swift:32 uses the same plain content. Tapping a notification opens Safari in a sheet over the feed (ContentView.swift:84-85) rather than the story's card. Inshorts and Google News push the headline as the title, the 60-word gist in an expanded view, a thumbnail, and Save/Share actions.
findings.recommendation: Title: the headline (max 70 characters). Body: the first sentence of the summary. Subtitle: 'The Verge · +3 outlets'. Download the 720px JPEG to a temp file in the background task and attach it with UNNotificationAttachment(identifier:url:options: [UNNotificationAttachmentOptionsThumbnailClippingRectKey: ...]). Set threadIdentifier = category.rawValue, relevanceScore from topRank, and interruptionLevel = .timeSensitive only for 4+ outlet stories (this needs the Time Sensitive entitlement, which is free). Register a UNNotificationCategory with 'Save' and 'Share' actions. A tap should deep-link to the card in the feed (set category, then scrollPosition = id), not open Safari. Server push via APNs is free with the dev account, and is what makes timing 'proper'; that belongs to the notifications dimension.

findings.title: Dynamic Type and VoiceOver: fixed-height card plus lineLimits break at large text sizes, and actions are not exposed as rotor actions
findings.evidence: The card is exactly one container high (ContentView.swift:118) with title .lineLimit(4) and body .lineLimit(10) plus minimumScaleFactor (CardView.swift:33,40-41), and there is no inner ScrollView. At AX1–AX5 sizes the summary drops to 2–3 lines and gets cut off. The source row .lineLimit(1) truncates '+N more' and the timestamp. VoiceOver reads source, '+N more', '·', time, title and body as separate elements. Save and Share are separate small icon buttons with no accessibilityAction on the card. The '·' Text (line 25) is read aloud.
findings.recommendation: For dynamicTypeSize >= .accessibility1, switch to a layout where the text block sits in a ScrollView inside the card and the image collapses to 120pt (use @Environment(\.dynamicTypeSize)). Cap the meta row with .dynamicTypeSize(...DynamicTypeSize.accessibility2). Make the text VStack .accessibilityElement(children: .combine), mark the dot .accessibilityHidden(true), and add .accessibilityAction(named: "Save"), .accessibilityAction(named: "Share") and .accessibilityAction(named: "Read full story") on the card. Give the icon buttons 44×44 hit areas (.frame(minWidth: 44, minHeight: 44).contentShape(Rectangle())); they currently size to the glyph.

findings.title: Saved, Settings and Share are bare system forms
findings.evidence: SavedView (SupportViews.swift:27-39) is a List of headline plus 'source · date', with no thumbnail, no summary and no search, and tapping goes straight to Safari. Settings (SupportViews.swift:90-96) lists 27 source toggles in 5 sections with no logos, and has no text-size, appearance, region or topic controls. The share sheet (ShareCard.swift) renders a decent image, but the text claims '60 words' and the photo is fetched again over the network on tap (line 17), so there is a visible spinner in the share button.
findings.recommendation: Saved: rows with a 64×64 rounded thumbnail, the headline in .headline, and source logo plus time in .footnote. Tapping opens the same card UI in a sheet with .presentationDetents([.large]), plus .searchable and a 'Clear all' action. Settings: group as 'Your feed' (topics and region, then a 'Manage sources' NavigationLink to a logo list), 'Notifications' (Morning brief time, Breaking alerts, Quiet hours), 'Reading' (Text size slider, Open links in Reader, Appearance), and 'About'. Share: reuse the image already loaded by ImageLoader, and change the copy to match the real word cap.

findings.title: No home-screen or lock-screen widget
findings.evidence: There is no widget extension in ios/Techgist.xcodeproj; the only Swift sources are App/, Views/, Services/ and Models/. Apple News, Google News and Inshorts all ship widgets, which are a main daily-return driver for headline apps.
findings.recommendation: Add a WidgetKit extension (free) that reads the cached ArticleCache from an App Group container. Ship 3 families: systemSmall (the top story's image with the headline overlaid), systemMedium (3 headlines with source logos and times) and accessoryRectangular for the lock screen (top headline). Use a TimelineProvider refresh every 30 min, matching the server cron, and widgetURL deep links to the card.

findings.title: Dark mode and small polish details
findings.evidence: The card shadow .black.opacity(0.08) (CardView.swift:81) disappears in dark mode, so cards blend into systemGroupedBackground. The StoryCover gradients use fixed RGB values (CardView.swift:111-115) that look neon on OLED black. The new-stories pill counts new stories across all categories, even when the current tab has none (NewsStore.swift:120), and never auto-dismisses. The navigation title 'Techgist' is plain inline text with no logo.
findings.recommendation: In dark mode, use a 0.5pt Color.white.opacity(0.08) stroke instead of a shadow, or go full-bleed. Desaturate the cover gradients under colorScheme == .dark. Compute newCount per current category, and show 'N new in AI' with a 'Top' fallback. Auto-hide the pill after 8s, and show it again on the next scroll-up. Put the logo plus wordmark in ToolbarItem(placement: .principal) as an HStack with Image("Logo") at 22pt and Text("Techgist").font(.headline).

verdict: Techgist doesn't really have a notification system. There is no APNs push, no aps-environment entitlement, no server sender and no Notification Service Extension. Every alert is a local notification created on the phone. The daily digest (DailyDigest.swift:20-36) is a repeating 8:00 calendar trigger whose text is fixed whenever the app last ran, so it can show the same old headline day after day. The 'big story' alert (BreakingNews.swift:40-58) can only fire inside a BGAppRefresh task. iOS runs those rarely and hours late for a new, little-used app, and never after the user swipes the app away. Even when one runs, the rule (3+ outlets and under 6 hours old, BreakingNews.swift:13,30-31) matches nothing in the live edition: at 03:30Z on 11 Nov, all 3 stories with 3+ outlets were 14.0h, 30.3h and 36.7h old. Outlets keep adding coverage for hours, so a story usually reaches 3 outlets after its 6-hour window has closed. When an alert does go out, it is plain: the publisher name as the title ('The Verge + 2 more'), the headline as the body, the default sound, no image, no subtitle, no thread, no actions, no relevance score. Tapping it opens Safari, not the in-app card. Apple News, Google News and Inshorts send server push through APNs, picked by editors or algorithms within minutes. Their alerts carry a large image added by a Notification Service Extension, a sharp headline plus summary, threads and collapse IDs, timing based on the user's time zone, quiet hours and frequency caps. That is the gap the owner feels. All of it can be built for free on what already exists. The Linux box sends pushes directly to APNs with a token-based .p8 key. A free Cloudflare Worker with D1 stores device tokens (or CloudKit's public database, or FCM topics; trade-offs below). An NSE attaches the 720px JPEG that enrich.py already makes. A detection step every 10-15 minutes decides what is breaking, using the time the server first saw a story rather than the publisher's date.

findings.title: No remote push at all: alerts depend on BGAppRefresh, which iOS runs rarely and late
findings.evidence: Techgist-Info.plist has UIBackgroundModes=[fetch] only, there is no .entitlements file (no aps-environment), and nothing calls registerForRemoteNotifications. BreakingNews.alertIfNeeded only runs from BackgroundRefresh.run (DailyDigest.swift:52-60). schedule() sets earliestBeginDate to +1h (DailyDigest.swift:46), but iOS decides the real time from app usage, Low Power Mode and the Background App Refresh switch, and never runs it after the user swipes the app away. The app's own Settings footer admits this: 'iOS decides when the app checks in the background, so alerts can arrive a few hours after a story breaks' (SupportViews.swift ~line 78).
findings.recommendation: Switch to server-sent APNs. (1) Owner, once: developer.apple.com > Certificates, IDs & Profiles > Keys > '+' > enable Apple Push Notifications service (APNs) > download AuthKey_XXXXXXXXXX.p8 (it can be downloaded only once). Note the Key ID and Team ID A4HLS6BV3C. In Xcode, add the Push Notifications capability to com.pranjald.techgist; this creates the aps-environment entitlement. (2) App: after authorization, call UIApplication.shared.registerForRemoteNotifications(). In application(_:didRegisterForRemoteNotificationsWithDeviceToken:), POST {token (hex), tz: TimeZone.current.identifier, briefMinute, breaking: Bool, env: 'production' or 'sandbox', appVersion} to the registry, again on every launch and whenever settings change. (3) Server: add push.py next to enrich.py (Python with httpx[http2] and PyJWT). Sign an ES256 JWT {iss: TeamID, iat} with header {kid: KeyID} and reuse it for 20-50 minutes; Apple rejects a token refreshed more than once every 20 minutes (TooManyProviderTokenUpdates) and one older than an hour. POST to https://api.push.apple.com/3/device/<token> (api.sandbox.push.apple.com for debug builds) with headers apns-topic: com.pranjald.techgist, apns-push-type: alert, apns-priority: 10, apns-expiration: now+4h for breaking or now+2h for the brief, apns-collapse-id: <story hash>. Delete the token from the registry on 410 Unregistered or 400 BadDeviceToken. The box only makes outbound HTTPS, so its private network is not a problem. Keep the local digest only as a fallback for users who have no token yet.

findings.title: Breaking-alert rule is wrong: 3 outlets and under 6h by publisher date almost never matches
findings.evidence: BreakingNews.swift:13 (minOutlets 3, maxAgeHours 6) and :30-31 measure age from publishedAt. In the live edition (published 2026-11-11T03:30Z), only 3 Top stories have 3+ outlets: 'Ring's Indoor Drone Camera Is Back' (3 outlets, 14.0h old), 'Claude Fable 5.2 and Mythos 5.2 cement Anthropic's AI lead' (4, 30.3h), 'Who is the suspected Chinese spy at centre of the Nvidia investigation?' (7, 36.7h). Zero match. Wider coverage comes later than the first report, so the two conditions rarely hold together. Also, a future-dated item (OpenAI, publishedAt 2026-11-12T00:00Z) gives a negative age and always passes the 6h check.
findings.recommendation: Move detection to the server and base it on when the server first saw a story. Keep ~/.techshorts/seen.json with {storyKey: firstSeenAt, outletsAt: [(outlet, time)]}. Breaking score = outlets that picked the story up within 3h of firstSeen (Reddit counts as one, as now) + 2 if a tier-1 outlet covered it (Verge, TechCrunch, Bloomberg, Reuters, NYT, CNBC, BBC) + HN velocity (points per hour > 100) + an LLM 'is this breaking for tech people? 0-1' score (ask nemotron in the same enrich call, a few tokens). Push when score >= threshold, firstSeen < 3h ago, and no breaking push in the last 3h. Cap each user at 2 breaking per day. Clamp publishedAt to min(publishedAt, firstSeenAt) to remove future dates. Run a light 'pulse' job every 10 minutes that fetches only the edition's tier-1 feeds plus the HN front page, with no LLM or image work. The README and publish.sh say the full publish runs every 2 hours ('17 */2 * * *'), which is too slow for anything called breaking.

findings.title: Daily digest is a repeating trigger with content fixed in advance, so stale headlines repeat
findings.evidence: DailyDigest.swift:31-35: UNCalendarNotificationTrigger(..., repeats: true) with body = top.displayTitle, set when reschedule() last ran. The 18h freshness check (line 26) runs when the notification is scheduled, not when it fires. If the user opens the app at 23:00 Monday and BGAppRefresh doesn't run, 08:00 Tuesday, Wednesday, Thursday... all show Monday's headline. Title is the fixed 'Your daily Techgist'; there's no image and no other stories.
findings.recommendation: Send the morning brief as a server push in each user's time zone: 08:00 local by default (IST 08:00 = 02:30Z; Pacific 08:00 = 16:00Z PST / 15:00Z PDT), with the time chosen in Settings. The registry stores tz and briefMinute; push.py runs every 15 minutes and sends to tokens whose local time falls in the current 15-minute slot. Bengaluru and the Bay Area then each get a brief built from the latest edition, not one from 13h earlier. Payload: title 'Wed brief · 5 stories', subtitle the #1 LLM headline, body '• <headline 2>\n• <headline 3>\n• <headline 4>', thread-id 'brief', relevance-score 0.6, mutable-content 1, image = the #1 story's 720px JPEG. Until push ships, at least change the fallback local digest to repeats: false and schedule it again on every refresh, so a stale headline fires at most once and then falls back to generic text.

findings.title: Device-token registry without a database: options compared honestly
findings.evidence: server/README.md: 'The server is on a private network, so phones never connect to it.' GitHub is read-only for phones; a write token in the app would leak. Settings footer (SupportViews.swift ~line 111): 'Your reading, saves and settings stay on this device.'
findings.recommendation: Recommended: a Cloudflare Worker with D1, on the free tier (100k requests/day; D1 5 GB). About 60 lines: POST /register upserts (token, tz, briefMinute, breaking, env, updatedAt). GET /tokens with a bearer secret, called only by the Linux box, returns active tokens. DELETE on 410. It works for every user, adds no SDK to the app, and gives full control. Alternative A: CloudKit public database. The app saves a CKRecord with the token; the Linux box reads it through CloudKit Web Services with a server-to-server key (ECDSA-signed requests). It's free and Apple-only, but writes fail when the user isn't signed into iCloud, and request signing is more fiddly. Alternative B: FCM topics. The app subscribes to topics such as 'breaking' and 'brief_0800_Asia_Kolkata'; the server sends one HTTP v1 request per topic, with no token storage and no APNs client code; the .p8 is uploaded to Firebase. It needs the least code, but adds the Firebase SDK, Google as a data processor and its installation ID to the privacy label. Rejected: GitHub as the store (needs a secret in the app) and opening a port on the Linux box (a Cloudflare Tunnel works, but it's another moving part). Whichever is chosen: update the App Store privacy label (Identifiers > Device ID, App Functionality, not linked, no tracking), change the Settings footer, and include in the privacy policy that a push token and time zone are stored to deliver notifications.

findings.title: Notification content is poor: publisher name as title, no image, summary or grouping
findings.evidence: BreakingNews.swift:45-50: title = '\(story.source) + \(others) more', body = displayTitle, sound .default, userInfo only {url}. No subtitle, threadIdentifier, categoryIdentifier, attachments, relevanceScore, interruptionLevel or targetContentIdentifier. The edition already has an LLM 'headline', a 55-70 word 'summary' and a 720px 'image' for 138 of 226 stories.
findings.recommendation: Breaking payload: {aps: {alert: {title: <LLM headline, ≤90 chars>, subtitle: 'Breaking · TechCrunch + 6 more', body: <60-word summary; iOS shows ~4 lines in the banner and all of it on long-press>}, sound: 'techgist.caf', 'mutable-content': 1, 'thread-id': 'breaking', 'relevance-score': 1.0, 'interruption-level': 'active', category: 'STORY', 'target-content-id': <storyId>}, storyId, url, image: <raw.githubusercontent.com/.../img/<hash>.jpg>}. Add a Notification Service Extension target (com.pranjald.techgist.NotificationService). didReceive downloads `image` into a temp .jpg, attaches UNNotificationAttachment(identifier:'img', url:, options: [UNNotificationAttachmentOptionsThumbnailClippingRectKey...]), and if the download fails, delivers anyway in serviceExtensionTimeWillExpire (the limit is about 30s and memory is tight, so keep the images ~100 KB like the current 720px JPEGs). Only stories with an LLM headline should go to push; skip the 23 without one.

findings.title: Tapping an alert opens Safari instead of the app's own story card
findings.evidence: AppDelegate.didReceive (BreakingNews.swift:81-86) gets only userInfo['url']; ContentView.swift:84-85 shows it in a SafariView sheet. The user leaves Techgist's 60-word format on the first tap.
findings.recommendation: Carry storyId in the payload. On tap: refresh the edition if it's stale, switch to the Top tab, scroll to that card (reuse ScrollViewReader and add a store.focus(id:)), and briefly highlight it with an animation. Show the publisher page only after the user taps 'Read more'. If the story isn't in the cached feed yet, insert it from the payload (headline, summary, image, url) so the card shows up instantly.

findings.title: Permission flow: one chance, asked too early, no provisional, no .badge, no way back
findings.evidence: ContentView.swift:74-81 shows the offer 20s after first launch and sets notificationsOffered=true before the user decides; 'Not now' (line 172) never asks again. Authorization options are [.alert, .sound] (DailyDigest.swift:16, BreakingNews.swift:17) with no .badge or .provisional. NotificationsOffer sets breakingNews from the digest grant (line 164), so both are off if denied.
findings.recommendation: Ask in context: after the user has swiped about 8 cards or saved a story, show the sheet with a real preview (a mock banner using that day's top headline and image). On 'Not now', request [.provisional] so quiet alerts land in Notification Center with Apple's own Keep/Turn Off buttons, and offer the full prompt again after 3 days or 3 sessions. Request [.alert, .sound, .badge]. Show the system status in Settings (getNotificationSettings) and link to openNotificationSettingsURLString when denied. This already exists for toggles; reuse it on the offer screen.

findings.title: No custom sound, categories/actions or threads, and in-app notifications skip Notification Center
findings.evidence: content.sound = .default (BreakingNews.swift:49, DailyDigest.swift:30). No setNotificationCategories call anywhere. willPresent returns [.banner, .sound] without .list (BreakingNews.swift:76-79), so alerts that arrive while the app is open are not kept in Notification Center.
findings.recommendation: Bundle techgist.caf in the main app (linear PCM or IMA4, under 30s; aim for a 0.4-0.8s soft two-note chime) and send 'sound': 'techgist.caf'. Register category 'STORY' with actions 'Save' (no foreground needed, writes to saved.json) and 'Share' (opens the app's ShareCard), plus hiddenPreviewsBodyPlaceholder '%u new stories' and a summary format for grouped threads. Return [.banner, .list, .sound] in willPresent, and for a breaking alert that matches the card on screen, suppress it and show the existing 'new stories' pill instead.

findings.title: Timing, frequency caps and quiet hours aren't modeled
findings.evidence: The only caps are 1 per refresh and 3 per day (BreakingNews.swift:13); there are no quiet hours or minimum gap, and the time zone isn't considered. Content freshness is limited by the CDN: raw.githubusercontent.com returns 'cache-control: max-age=300', and the cron publishes every 2h.
findings.recommendation: Server-side policy per token: at most 1 brief and 2 breaking per day, at least 3h between breaking pushes, no breaking pushes 22:00-07:30 local (hold for the next brief instead), apns-collapse-id so a story that picks up more outlets updates its alert instead of sending a duplicate, and apns-expiration so night-time breaking alerts don't show up 8h later. Track opens: the app reports the storyId it opened to the Worker, anonymously, so the threshold can be tuned. Stay away from 'time-sensitive' (it needs the com.apple.developer.usernotifications.time-sensitive entitlement, and Apple's guidance reserves it for alerts needing immediate action); 'active' with relevance-score is enough. App Review 4.5.4: push must not be required to use the app and must not be used for marketing; this design meets both.

verdict: The server is a sensible first version. One cron job runs the app's own Swift feed code, an LLM adds headlines and summaries afterwards, and the result is pushed to a branch with a single amended commit. But it is not a news pipeline yet, and most of the "cheap copy" feeling in the app traces back to it. The LLM only rewrites text; all selection is done by headline-token heuristics. That fails badly on live data. The current edition (published 2026-11-11T03:30Z: 226 stories, 585 KB) has about 9 separate Anthropic IPO cards in Top (topRanks 7, 9, 22, 26, 36, 52 and 63 are near-duplicate IPO stories; 3, 38 and 82 are other Anthropic news). 211 of 226 stories show coverage of 1, so the "3+ outlets" breaking-news rule almost never fires. Product Hunt launches like "Clive" and "Obsiva" go out as news, and an OpenAI post dated 20 hours in the future sits first in the newest-first Top tab. AI coverage is 160/226 (71%), and only 75/104 (72%) in Top. Whole sources get none: NYT 0/8, OpenAI 0/12, Product Hunt 0/12. Those skips are cached for 7 days and never retried. So the reader sees raw publisher headlines and 5–25 word excerpts mixed in with 65-word cards. From a publisher posting to the story appearing in the app typically takes 30–60+ minutes; for a notification it takes hours, because alerts come only from on-device BGAppRefresh. There is no push, no per-tab payload, no schema version, no health signal, and the docs disagree on cadence (publish.sh:4 and the README say 2 h; the task says 30 min). Inshorts and Google News run a server that triages, clusters, writes and pushes. Within the constraints the right upgrade is a long-running Python worker on the Linux box. It polls feeds every 2–5 minutes with conditional GETs. Each new item gets one LLM triage call that returns category, importance score, junk flag, event key for dedupe, headline and summary, and a story is publishable only if it has AI text. It publishes small versioned per-tab files every few minutes, sends APNs pushes for score ≥ 8 events directly from the box, and writes a health.json.

findings.title: Same-story clustering fails: ~9 Anthropic IPO cards in Top, coverage signal is almost always 1
findings.evidence: Ranker.swift:125-130 groups stories only when they share 3 or more title tokens with an IDF overlap of at least 0.4. In the live edition the Top ranks 7, 9, 22, 26, 36, 52 and 63 are near-duplicate Anthropic IPO stories (Guardian, CNBC x2, NYT x2, BBC, TechCrunch), and 38 and 82 are other Anthropic news. Coverage counts across 226 stories: 211 have 1, 9 have 2, 1 has 3, 3 have 4, 2 have 7. One cluster even joins a BBC news story with a Stratechery blog post. BreakingNews.swift:13 needs minOutlets=3, so alerts almost never qualify.
findings.recommendation: Move dedupe to the server and base it on meaning. For each new item, ask the LLM for an `event_key`: a short canonical slug such as `anthropic-ipo-pricing-2026-11`. Give it the last 48 h of existing event keys and headlines in the prompt so it can reuse one. Also do a cheap embedding check: NVIDIA hosts nv-embedqa / llama-3.2-nv-embedqa on the same key; treat cosine ≥ 0.85 within 48 h as the same event. Publish one card per event, with `sources:[...]` and `coverage=n`, and pick the lead by source trust and the best AI text. Keep the token heuristic only as an offline fallback.

findings.title: No server-side triage: junk and non-news ship, and categories are fixed per feed
findings.evidence: Category comes from the feed (FeedService.swift:115). The junk filter is a regex (FeedService.swift:123-138). In the live edition, 12 Product Hunt items ('Clive', 'Inspo by Context.dev', 'Obsiva', 'ZUS', 'Daytwo'...) and 12 DEV Community posts appear as news, and two DEV posts are among the newest in Top. The NYT item 'What BlackBerries and Horseshoes Reveal About Our Presidents' and 'A Fan-Favorite Aquarium Screen Saver Is Leaving Roku' are off-topic for Bengaluru/SV tech readers. Ranker.score (Ranker.swift:64-70) has no signal for importance or audience.
findings.recommendation: Add one LLM triage call per new item, merged with the summary call into one JSON reply: {category: AI|Startups|Dev|Big Tech|India|Policy|Blogs, importance: 1-10, audience_fit: 1-10, is_news: bool, junk_reason, event_key, headline, summary, india_relevance: bool}. Drop items where is_news is false or junk_reason is set, and keep Product Hunt or DEV only if importance ≥ 7. Rank by importance × coverage boost × source weight / (age_h+6), and send this as a server-computed per-tab order; the app currently re-sorts by publishedAt (NewsStore.swift:47), which throws ranking away. Add Indian sources (Inc42, YourStory, Moneycontrol Tech, ET Tech) for the Bengaluru audience.

findings.title: AI text covers only 71% of stories; whole sources never get it, and failures are cached for 7 days
findings.evidence: Live: 160/226 stories have headline+summary, and 75/104 in Top. Top #0 (NYT Toyota) and #2 (Wired Ring drone) have none. By source: New York Times 0/8 (paywall, so the RSS excerpt is under the 40-word gate at enrich.py:124), OpenAI 0/12 (bot-blocked pages), Product Hunt 0/12. enrich.py:179-180 caches every skip except 'model failed' (too little text, a length miss, or a failed grounding check), and the cache prune at enrich.py:195 keeps live stories, so those stories never get retried. MAX_NEW_PER_RUN=80 (line 23) also leaves a backlog after a cold start. Fallback cards show 5–25 word excerpts (median 24.5 words) next to 65-word AI cards.
findings.recommendation: Make AI text a publish gate: a story without a validated headline+summary is not shown. Tiers: (1) full article text; (2) if under 40 words, write a short summary (25–40 words) from feed text, title and meta description, marked as brief; (3) if grounding fails, retry once, feeding back the offending tokens ('do not use X'); (4) still failing, hold and retry next cycle, up to 3 tries, then drop. Cache skips with a reason and attempt count, and give each skip a TTL of 1 h instead of 7 days. Relax grounding for proper nouns that appear in the original title or source name (already partly done), and allow common names such as country, company and month names. Log skip reasons by source.

findings.title: End-to-end freshness is 30–60+ min at best, and alerts arrive hours late
findings.evidence: The path is: cron cadence (30 min per the task; publish.sh:4 and the README say 2 h) + run time (sequential feed fetch, Reddit retry with a fixed 35 s sleep at main.swift:78, metadata batches of 8, enrichment with 4 threads where each item waits up to 15 s for the page plus up to 3×90 s for the LLM, then sequential thumbnails up to 20 s each at enrich.py:185-190) + raw.githubusercontent cache-control max-age=300 (measured: 'x-cache: HIT', 'source-age: 11') + the app's foreground staleAfter of 15 min (NewsStore.swift:27). Background refresh asks for earliestBeginDate +3600 (DailyDigest.swift:46), and iOS often defers it by hours. Breaking alerts are local notifications from that refresh (BreakingNews.swift), so they lag by hours.
findings.recommendation: Replace cron with a systemd service running a loop. Fetch feeds every 3 min with ETag/If-Modified-Since (most feeds return 304, which is cheap). Enrich new items immediately, with up to 8 concurrent LLM calls. Publish when there are changes, at most every 5 min. Raw CDN max-age=300 then dominates (about 5–10 min end to end). For alerts, send APNs from the Linux box using the existing developer account: token-based .p8 auth over HTTP/2 to api.push.apple.com, sent to an 'breaking' topic via device tokens. Collect tokens with a free Cloudflare Worker + KV, or a GitHub-issue-free endpoint on a free tier. Or, with no token collection at all, use APNs broadcast channels (iOS 18+). A server push lets you send at the right moment, with the right sound and a rich image.

findings.title: Monolithic 585 KB edition with full article text; no per-tab files, pagination or schema version
findings.evidence: Live edition.json is 584,583 bytes (194 KB gzipped). 364,754 bytes of it are `content` (up to 1000 words of body per story, FeedService.swift:112), which the app only uses for on-device summaries that the server now writes anyway. There is no `schemaVersion` or `editionId`, and Edition.swift:5-8 decodes {publishedAt, articles}. Every foreground refresh re-downloads it with .reloadIgnoringLocalCacheData (FeedService.swift:26), which also ignores ETag. The app also re-sorts tabs by date instead of using the server's order.
findings.recommendation: Publish `v2/manifest.json` (about 1 KB: schemaVersion, editionId, publishedAt, per-tab etags, minAppVersion, killSwitch/banner) plus `v2/top.json`, `v2/ai.json` and so on, each holding the 40–60 cards for that tab in ranked order, with only the fields the cards need (id, headline, summary, image, source, sources, coverage, importance, publishedAt, url, breaking flag). Drop `content` and `excerpt` when AI text exists. Expected size is about 40–60 KB per tab. The app fetches the manifest first and fetches tabs only when their etag changes, using the default cache policy so 304s work. Keep v1 edition.json in place until 1.2 users are gone.

findings.title: Image pipeline: rotated filenames break cached and saved stories; 94 KB images; slow raw host
findings.evidence: enrich.py:191-192 deletes every image not in the current edition, and the branch is a single amended force-push (publish.sh:62-69). Article URLs held in ArticleCache and in saved.json (NewsStore saved) then 404: the image directory root on raw.githubusercontent.com already returns 404, and any URL pruned from the branch would too. One sampled thumbnail was 94,246 bytes and took 75.5 s from this network. Thumbnails are generated sequentially, there is no WebP/HEIC, and 7 Top stories have no image.
findings.recommendation: Keep images for 14 days (prune by mtime, not by membership in the edition) so cached and saved cards don't break. Encode at 720 px with quality 60–65 progressive JPEG (about 45–60 KB), and add a 360 px variant for list rows. Generate thumbnails in parallel with enrichment. Serve images from GitHub Pages on the same branch (Pages is already prepared per the README) or Cloudflare R2's free tier (10 GB, no egress fees) for better caching than raw. When a story has no image, render a branded image server-side instead of leaving it blank: a gradient with a source logo and an event-category glyph.

findings.title: Timestamp sanity missing: future-dated and very old items
findings.evidence: Live: an OpenAI story with publishedAt 2026-11-12T00:00:00Z was 20 h in the future at fetch time ('Gilbert + Tobin rethinks the business of law with AI'). Since the app sorts newest first, it is pinned to the top of Top. Blogs are allowed to be 45 days old (FeedService.swift:76), and the oldest story in the edition is 887 h (37 days) old. BBC stories 60–75 h old are still in Top.
findings.recommendation: On the server: clamp publishedAt to min(feedDate, firstSeenAt) and record `firstSeenAt` for each item. Cap Top at 36 h and other tabs at 72 h (blogs 7 days), with an importance-based exception: allow importance ≥ 8 up to 72 h in Top.

findings.title: Silent failure modes and no observability
findings.evidence: enrich.py:203-206 swallows every exception and still publishes. publish.sh:46-48 ends a failed enrich with an echo. main.swift:45 refuses to publish below 60 stories. If the edition is more than 8 h old (Edition.swift:10), the app silently falls back to fetching feeds directly, losing AI text, images, ranking and Reddit. The only health check is tailing publish.log on a private box. Nobody is alerted when the NVIDIA key expires, a feed dies (FeedService failures are only printed) or AI coverage drops.
findings.recommendation: Write `v2/health.json` on every publish: per-source fetch status and item count, AI coverage overall and per tab, a histogram of skip reasons, LLM p50/p95 latency and 429 count, run duration, and edition age. Add a check that sends you an ntfy.sh or Telegram-bot alert (both free) when AI coverage in Top falls below 95%, any source fails 3 runs in a row, or the edition is older than 20 min. Lower the app's fallback threshold to 2 h, and show a stale banner instead of silently switching origin.

findings.title: NVIDIA API usage: no rate budget, retries are blunt, prompt is not reused for triage
findings.evidence: ask() makes up to 3 tries with a 90 s timeout and a fixed sleep of 10/20/30 s on 429 (enrich.py:103-118), across 4 threads. There is no tokens or requests-per-minute accounting. Article text is capped at 1,500 words (line 83), roughly 2.5k input tokens per call. About 30 new items arrive per 30 min, so roughly 1.5k calls a day, which should fit NVIDIA's free/developer tier (about 40 RPM), but nothing enforces that. Model failures retry the next run with no backoff state.
findings.recommendation: Use a token bucket (for example 30 RPM) shared by all workers, honor Retry-After, and use a 30 s timeout. Send one combined triage+write call per item, with JSON mode or a schema and an 800-word input cap; the lead paragraphs carry the news. Keep a second model as a fallback (for example a larger Nemotron or Llama on the same API) for items that fail grounding twice. Log tokens per call to health.json.

findings.title: Editorial controls are file edits on a private box with no fast path
findings.evidence: editorial.json supports only `pinned` (a full Story object) and `blocked` (a substring of source or URL) (main.swift:10-24). Changes apply on the next cron run. There is no way to boost or bury a story, mark one as breaking, fix an AI headline or summary, or send an alert by hand.
findings.recommendation: Add an `editorial` section the worker reloads each loop: `boost:{url: +score}`, `bury:[url]`, `override:{url:{headline,summary}}`, `breaking:[url]` (sends a push), plus `holdUntilReview:true` for the first weeks. Expose it as a tiny CLI (`tg pin <url>`, `tg push <url>`) on the box, and later as a private GitHub issue/label watcher (free) so you can curate from your phone.

verdict: Best-in-class news apps all share one idea that Techgist lacks: an edited, finite edition. They pick a small number of event clusters, write each one to a fixed length, place them by importance and freshness, and send 2-3 well-timed pushes a day. Techgist has the parts (clustering in Ranker.swift, LLM rewriting in enrich.py, a 30-minute server cron), but it shows the raw firehose. The live edition (publishedAt 2026-11-11T03:30Z) has 226 articles. 104 of them carry a topRank, and the Top tab holds 91 cards, some up to 74 hours old. The same event appears many times: the Anthropic IPO shows up as at least 9 separate Top cards (ranks 7, 9, 22, 26, 36, 52, 63, plus more in AI and Blogs), and the Nvidia/Jensen Huang spy story as 8 (ranks 10, 53, 67, 72, 73, 83, 87, 95). Google News, Particle and Techmeme would show each of these as one card with a 'Full coverage' / '+12 sources' expander. Length is off too: Inshorts holds a strict 60 words, but Techgist's LLM summaries run 39-99 words (median 65), and 66 of 226 stories have no LLM summary at all and fall back to a cut-off RSS excerpt. Some of those fallbacks are junk, such as the HN item whose excerpt begins with 'Previously: .name Termination - https://news.ycombinator.com/...'. Freshness and notifications are the weakest part. Inshorts and Apple News publishers send server-timed pushes capped at about 3 a day (Apple: 3/day mixed, hard cap 5, 10-95 characters). Techgist relies on BGAppRefresh local notifications that iOS may run hours late, with no image and the default sound (BreakingNews.swift:47-53). Its 'daily digest' repeats one headline at a fixed time (DailyDigest.swift:28-36). The app has no India sources for a Bengaluru audience (no Inc42, YourStory, Entrackr, ET Tech, Moneycontrol in FeedSource.swift), and its cards are a plain image-plus-text layout with stock SwiftUI animation and no haptics. All of these gaps can be fixed on the existing free stack. APNs token auth needs only the Apple developer account, the Linux box can already send HTTP/2, and NVIDIA's LLM can do cluster labelling and 60-word rewrites.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Inshorts (incl. tech section)
findings.evidence: App Store listing and company pages: 60-word 'shorts'. The CEO's stated rationale is that readers decide within two sentences whether a story interests them. The content team writes 70-80 stories a day (older figure; now 'hundreds' across all categories), and a tech reader sees perhaps 10-20 a day. Notifications are described as 'limited daily notifications for the most important and breaking news'; a third-party source says 2-3 a day (unverified). Card anatomy: image on the top ~40%, a human-written headline of 1-2 lines, exactly 60 words of body, a source line ('short by <editor> / <time>'), and a bottom strip 'swipe left for more at <Source>'. Vertical swipe goes between stories, horizontal swipe opens the source. Feeds: My Feed (learns from swipes), All News, Top Stories, Trending, Bookmarks, plus per-topic tabs including Technology and Startup. Also 'TOSS' sharing to friends, polls, and search over old shorts. Users complain about ads and crashes, so Techgist can beat it on polish.
findings.recommendation: Copy these: (1) a hard 60-word body (55-62 words, enforced in enrich.py with a word count check and a retry); (2) a headline of 70 characters or less, readable in one glance; (3) each card is self-contained, so the reader never needs to tap through; (4) a 'swipe left = open source' gesture with a bottom strip 'More at The Verge >'; (5) 2-3 notifications a day; (6) a 'Startups' tab that leads with Indian startups.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Apple News (incl. notifications)
findings.evidence: Apple's News publisher notification guide: up to 3 notifications a day for mixed breaking and non-breaking alerts, a hard cap of 5, non-breaking-only senders at 2 a day; copy 10-95 characters; 'better to be right than first'; every alert deep-links to the article in-app. Today feed: an editor-curated 'Top Stories' block (about 5-6 stories), then 'Trending', then 'For You' groups by topic, ending with a 'You're all caught up' style end state. The large lead card uses a full-bleed image and a bold serif headline; secondary cards are compact rows with a thumbnail. Apple News Today is a daily briefing of about 6-8 stories. Rich notification UI shows the publisher logo plus an image thumbnail.
findings.recommendation: Adopt Apple's numbers as Techgist's notification policy: at most 3 alerts a day, alert copy 10-95 characters, each alert opens the in-app card (not Safari), and a 'Top 5' lead block before the stream. Use a typographic hierarchy: one hero card per session, then compact cards.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Google News
findings.evidence: Google says its systems analyze news across the web to choose top stories for everyone with the same language and country settings, and that Top stories are not personalized. 'For you' is the personalized section. Each story is a cluster: one lead article, 3-4 alternate headlines from other outlets, and a 'Full Coverage' button opening a timeline, perspectives, FAQs and fact checks, sortable by relevance or time. Briefing: about 5 top stories at the top of For You, labelled by time of day. Clusters collapse to one headline except the top story.
findings.recommendation: Make Techgist's Top tab a list of clusters, not articles. Each cluster gets one card with an LLM-written neutral headline and 60 words, plus a 'Full coverage (9)' sheet listing every outlet with its own title and timestamp. Today's live edition would drop from 91 Top cards to about 30-40 events.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Particle
findings.evidence: Per a competitor-published report, Particle ingests about 60k articles a day from 50k+ outlets, groups them into story clusters, and has editors review the AI summaries. It offers summary modes: default bullet points, '5Ws', 'Explain Like I'm 5', 'Opposite Sides'. It also has a per-story Q&A chat, audio summaries, and a StandBy/CarPlay headline widget (October 2025 changelog). Cards show a 3-bullet summary, an outlet logo stack ('12 sources'), and a 'story is developing' label when new articles join the cluster.
findings.recommendation: Generate 3 bullets of 15 words or less per cluster alongside the 60-word paragraph, and let the user toggle between them with a tap. Add a source logo stack (up to 4 favicons plus '+N'). Add a 'Developing · 3 new updates' chip when the cluster grew since the last view. Skip chat.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Artifact (shut down Jan 2024)
findings.evidence: Artifact was built by Instagram's founders, used ML personalization from reading time, and added AI summaries and an AI rewrite of clickbait headlines (this search did not confirm the rewrite feature). Downloads fell from about 444k in February 2023 to about 12k by October 2023, per a report citing Appfigures. It drifted from a news reader into social posting and links and closed; the founders said the market was not big enough.
findings.recommendation: Lessons: personalization alone does not create retention, and adding social features did not save Artifact. Keep the core reader tight. Do copy the 'reads' signal (dwell time per card) to quietly reweight topics, and keep the headline-rewrite instruction (no questions, no teasers, state the news) in enrich.py.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Techmeme
findings.evidence: Hybrid model since 2008. Algorithms score stories by links and age; editors gate every top-level headline and write headlines (since 2013). Each item is one lead link with a rewritten headline in the form 'Source: Fact-dense sentence with numbers'. 'More:' lists 5-30 discussing outlets and X/Bluesky posts. Rank is by importance, and big stories stay on top for 12-24 hours while second-tier stories rotate. Daily volume is about 30-50 top-level items. Silicon Valley insiders read it as the tech 'paper of record'.
findings.recommendation: Use Techmeme's headline style for the target users: fact-first, number-dense, with the company as subject ('Anthropic targets up to $1.4T valuation in Nasdaq IPO, down from $2T talk'). Rank clusters by how many distinct publishers cover them, weighted by authority and decayed by age. Let mega-clusters stay pinned with updates rather than reappearing as new cards.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Ground News
findings.evidence: A story page shows a neutral AI summary on top, then full coverage, then a bias bar (Left/Center/Right percentages) and factuality ratings. A 'Blindspot' feed lists stories covered by only one side, 6 a day on the free tier. There is also a Daily Briefing on the home page.
findings.recommendation: Political bias does not fit tech news, but the coverage-meter pattern does. On each cluster card, show a small bar 'Covered by 9 outlets · first reported 5h ago by CNBC'. A tech-flavoured 'Blindspot' idea: an 'Under the radar' slot with 1-2 high-HN-points stories that mainstream outlets ignored.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - TLDR / Morning Brew newsletters
findings.evidence: TLDR: one edition at 6 AM ET on weekdays, built to take about 5 minutes. It has 10-15 items in themed sections (Big Tech & Startups, Science & Futuristic Tech, Programming/Design/Data Science, Miscellaneous), each a bold headline with '(N minute read)' plus 2-3 sentences, about 1,300 words in all. Subject lines stack 3 headlines ('Anthropic S-1 leaks, Tesla-SpaceX merger talks, ...'). Morning Brew (from general knowledge, not this search) uses a witty voice, a markets ticker up top, and a closing 'Brew's Bets' and quiz. Their retention comes from a fixed daily ritual time, a finite edition, and a known end.
findings.recommendation: Build a 'Morning Gist' edition: 10-12 clusters in 3 sections (AI, Startups & Money, Dev), each 60 words with a read-time chip. Publish it at 8:00 IST for Bengaluru and 7:00 PT for the Bay Area. Its push subject line is 3 stacked headlines, and it ends with an 'All caught up · 4 min read today' screen.

findings.title: COMPETITOR TEARDOWN - Hacker News readers (Harmonic, Hack, Octal, Materialistic)
findings.evidence: From general knowledge, not this search: these readers show points and comment count prominently ('715 pts · 412 comments'), domain, and age; some show an AI 'TL;DR of the discussion' or the top comment. Techgist already stores points (live edition: '.name Grandfathered' 715 pts) but not comments, and its card only shows points as a ranking factor.
findings.recommendation: For Dev/HN items, show a chip '715 pts · 412 comments on HN'. Have enrich.py write one extra line, 'HN says: ...', summarizing the top 20 comments (fetched from the Algolia HN API, which is free).
